CALIFORNIA RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT
(STANDARD MULTI-PAGE FORM)

THIS RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT ("Lease") is made and entered into this 15th day of August, 2025, by and between Pacific Coast Holdings, LP ("Landlord" or "Lessor"), and Marcus Vance and Sarah Vance ("Tenant" or "Lessee").

1. PREMISES
Landlord leases to Tenant and Tenant leases from Landlord the residential premises consisting of a 2-bedroom condominium located at 742 Ocean Boulevard, Unit 4C, Santa Monica, California 90401 ("Premises"), together with assigned parking space #24.

2. LEASE TERM
The term of this Lease shall commence on September 1, 2025 ("Commencement Date") and shall continue as a lease for term through August 31, 2026 ("Expiration Date"). Any extension or renewal shall be in writing signed by both parties at least sixty (60) days prior to the Expiration Date. If Tenant remains in possession after expiration with Landlord's consent, the tenancy shall convert to a month-to-month tenancy terminable by either party upon thirty (30) days written notice.

3. RENT PAYMENT AND LATE CHARGES
A. Monthly Rent: Tenant agrees to pay Landlord monthly base rent of $3,450.00, payable in advance on or before the first (1st) day of each calendar month.
B. Method of Payment: Payments shall be made via electronic ACH portal or cashier's check payable to Landlord. Cash is strictly not accepted.
C. Grace Period & Late Charge: Tenant acknowledges that late payment causes Landlord to incur administrative costs. If rent is not received by Landlord by 11:59 PM on the fifth (5th) day of the month, Tenant shall pay an additional late charge of $175.00. Any returned check or dishonored ACH shall incur a fee of $40.00.

4. SECURITY DEPOSIT
A. Deposit Amount: Prior to occupancy, Tenant shall deposit with Landlord the sum of $3,450.00 as a Security Deposit pursuant to California Civil Code Section 1950.5.
B. Use of Deposit: The Security Deposit may be applied by Landlord only for purposes reasonably necessary to: (i) remedy defaults in rent; (ii) repair damages to the premises caused by Tenant exclusive of ordinary wear and tear; and (iii) clean the premises upon termination of tenancy to the condition at move-in.
C. Return of Deposit: Within twenty-one (21) calendar days after Tenant has vacated the Premises and surrendered keys, Landlord shall furnish Tenant with an itemized written statement showing the basis for, and the amount of, any deductions, together with the remaining balance of the Security Deposit.

5. CONDITION OF PREMISES AND HABITABILITY
Tenant has examined the Premises, including all appliances, fixtures, smoke alarms, and carbon monoxide detectors, and acknowledges that they are in good, safe, and clean working condition. Landlord shall comply with all statutory obligations of habitability pursuant to California Civil Code Sections 1941 and 1941.1.

6. MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS
A. Landlord Obligations: Landlord shall maintain and repair the roof, exterior walls, foundations, heating system, electrical wiring, and primary plumbing facilities, unless damage is caused by Tenant's intentional act or gross negligence.
B. Tenant Obligations: Tenant shall keep the Premises in a clean and sanitary condition, promptly report all leaks or mechanical failures to Landlord in writing, dispose of all trash, and replace standard interior light bulbs and smoke detector batteries. Tenant shall be financially liable for drain blockages caused by improper disposal of grease or foreign objects.

7. ENTRY BY LANDLORD
Pursuant to California Civil Code Section 1954, Landlord or Landlord's authorized representatives may enter the Premises only under the following circumstances:
(a) In case of emergency;
(b) To make necessary or agreed repairs, alterations, or improvements;
(c) To exhibit the Premises to prospective purchasers, lenders, or tenants;
(d) When Tenant has abandoned or surrendered the Premises.
Except in cases of emergency or abandonment, Landlord shall provide Tenant with at least twenty-four (24) hours advance written notice of intention to enter, and entry shall take place only during standard business hours (8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday through Friday), unless Tenant expressly consents otherwise.

8. UTILITIES
Tenant shall be responsible for and pay directly for all electricity, gas, internet, and cable television services. Landlord shall pay for water, trash collection, and standard municipal sewer charges.

9. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING
Tenant shall not assign this Lease, nor sublet all or any portion of the Premises, nor allow any guest to reside in the Premises for more than fourteen (14) consecutive days or twenty-eight (28) days in any calendar year, without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

10. PET POLICY
No animals, birds, or pets of any kind shall be kept on the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent and execution of a Pet Addendum, with the exception of verified service animals or emotional support animals required by applicable disability law.

11. DEFAULT AND REMEDIES
If Tenant fails to pay rent when due or breaches any material term of this Lease, Landlord may issue a statutory Three-Day Notice to Pay Rent or Quit pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 1161. If Tenant fails to cure within the statutory three-day period, Landlord may initiate unlawful detainer legal proceedings to recover possession, past due rent, and statutory damages.

12. ATTORNEY'S FEES
In any legal action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Lease, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover reasonable attorney's fees and court costs from the non-prevailing party, up to a maximum cap of $2,500.00.

13. STATUTORY DISCLOSURES
A. Lead-Based Paint: Built after 1978; no known lead paint hazards.
B. Megan's Law Notice: Pursuant to Section 290.46 of the Penal Code, information about specified registered sex offenders is made available to the public via the California Department of Justice website (www.meganslaw.ca.gov).
C. Bed Bug Disclosure: Landlord provides information regarding bed bug prevention pursuant to Civil Code Section 1954.603.
